newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul reopens door for business deals in N.Korea.
newsitem.headline: Seoul reopens door for business deals in N.Korea.

text.p: South Korea opened the door for domestic companies to do business in rival North Korea on Friday for the first time since a submarine incursion in September shut off all contact.
The Unification Ministry said in a statement it had given approval to seven domestic companies to contact North Koreans for business ranging from garment making to soft drinks.
It said companies included trading firm LG International Corp, garment maker Shin Won Corp, drug maker Korea Green Cross Corp, and sewn goods maker Taechang Co Ltd.
All contacts with Pyongyang were frozen after a North Korean Shark-class submarine dropped 26 intruders on a Southern beach last September.

But Pyongyang issued a rare apology last month for the incident and Seoul returned the remains of 24 of the infiltrators who were shot and killed. One was captured alive and the other is still at large.
There have been few business deals between the two Koreas, which remain technically at war after their 1950-53 conflict ended in a truce and not in a peace agreement.
Seoul first allowed business links with the communist North in the late 1980s in the hope contact could thaw decades of hostility.
Business projects there have so far been focused on the processing-on-consignment of garments, bags and sewn goods while North Korea has sold some raw materials to the South.
The Stalinist state's economy has shrunk in recent years, partly due to the collapse of the Soviet Union, its former main benefactor.
North Korea is also suffering from severe food shortages after two years of floods. International aid agencies have said the shortages could worsen.

On Thursday, Pyongyang's official media said the country "set it as the central task of socialist economic construction this year to tap and utilise the economic potentials to the maximum, decidedly solve the food problem, radically improve the people's standard of living, promote land administration and lay a solid foundation for the prosperity of the country."
The Korea Central News Agency (KCNA) also said: "The rural economy is confronted with a task to do scientific and technical farming this year... and increase production of rice and meat."
